notes: Partition verified: all 20 source ids (s001-s020) and all 36 target ids (t001-t036) appear exactly once across the 21 units; no invented ids.

Status legality verified: the single non-aligned unit is the `added` t027-t029 (empty source, null source head, target head a member). No unrepresented or noncompositional units are claimed, and none is owed here.

οὐχ → *no* aligned rather than emptied is right: rules 41 and 59 empty a negator only before a second **negative** word, and τόπον is a plain noun. Rule 59's joining arm does not reach it either, since that arm wants a plain indefinite (τις/τι) fused into one English word; here the ASV writes *no* and *place* separately, so rule 2 splits them. Rule 87 is not in question, no πᾶς standing.
μετά + δακρύων correctly split under rule 94 (two English words, so no compound unit), with *with* on the preposition per rule 36 and the anarthrous noun keeping its own word.

The supplied *when* and *he* on θέλων are rule 7 helpers licensed by the participle under rule 86, not `added`; the discontinuity around t008 *afterward* is permitted by rule 15. Same for *he* on ἐκζητήσας around t033 *it*.

The `added` *in his father* is correctly not rule 37 (no neighbouring-verse Greek) and not rule 97 (no FALLBACK EXCLUDED mark in the packet); αὐτήν is already spent on t033, so rule 103's reasoning also points to `added`.
ὅτι is aligned to an expressed *that*, which is rule 43's own test (an English word is present), so the unrepresented arm is rightly not taken.

The head of the μετανοίας unit (*change* vs *mind*) is the one genuinely open choice. Rule 91's lemma query returns nothing usable here — the corpus glosses μετάνοια/μετανοέω as *repentance*/*repent*, neither English word — and both *change* and *mind* answer to an element of the compound, so rule 16 is satisfied by the note naming the competing reading. Left as accepted.
Minor wording only, not corrected because it changes nothing: the ἀπεδοκιμάσθη note calls the English *rejected* a participle; the head choice it records is right under rule 9 regardless.
The verse's alternative-rendering note (*no place of repentance* as one parenthesis) affects punctuation only and leaves the token-level alignment adopted here untouched.
